links.citation: The developer asks users to cite the Phi-4-reasoning Technical Report.

possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card provides only high-level architecture and post-training description, with no reported evaluations or details of the RL/safety SFT process, so inner workings and evaluation evidence are undocumented.

possible_risks.description: Proper documentation contains information about how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, including any synthetic data generation processes. Without proper documentation it might be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card states only an offline dataset with cutoff March 2025 and earlier, without collection, curation, or composition details, so training data transparency is limited.

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: Open-weight text-output reasoning model with no reported factual accuracy or grounding evaluations, so plausible hallucination risk in generated reasoning chains.

possible_risks.description: In AI-assisted decision-making tasks, reliance measures how much a person trusts (and potentially acts on) a model's output. Over-reliance occurs when a person puts too much trust in a model, accepting a model's output when the model's output is likely incorrect. Under-reliance is the opposite, where the person doesn't trust the model but should.
possible_risks.justification: Reasoning model outputs are likely to be trusted by users, but the card reports no calibration or human-AI decision-making evaluation, so over-reliance risk is plausible.

possible_risks.description: Since foundation models can be used for many purposes, a model's intended use is important for defining the relevant risks of that model. As the use changes, the relevant risks might correspondingly change.
possible_risks.justification: Card labels it a general reasoning model and gives no intended-use or out-of-scope use cases, leaving downstream risk assessment incomplete.

specifications.model_size: 27.3 GiB of safetensors weights (29,319,042,992 bytes) in BF16

training_context.adaptations: Phi-4-reasoning is a supervised fine-tuned and reinforcement learning post-trained reasoning model derived from Phi-4, with additional safety post-training via supervised fine-tuning.
training_context.data_cutoff: Static model trained on an offline dataset with cutoff dates of March 2025 and earlier for publicly available data
